summary: Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Bonn, completing his Ph.D. under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He served at the University of Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and full professor (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Macalester College, Harvard University, and Columbia University. He served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and Director of the South Asia Center at the University of Washington (2007).

Christian Lindtner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen by 1982. He also served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna (Magister 1994, Ph.D. 1998) and held posts at the Rubin Museum of Art (curator, 2012) and SOAS University of London (Senior Lecturer, 2014).
Christian Mabel Duff was an Indology scholar who studied at Kiel University under Paul Deussen.

Christian Matthias Boehm works in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied under Toshifumi Konno and earned degrees from SOAS, Technical University of Munich, Imperial College London, and Cambridge, later working at the Max Planck Institute (2017–2018) and the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (2019).

Christian Schweigaard Stang was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1918–1927) under Sten Konow and Antoine Meillet, later serving at Oslo as Associate Professor (1930) and Professor of Slavic Philology (1938–1970).

Christian Wittern is a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields who studied under Seizan Yanagida. He was an Associate Researcher at Chunghwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (1998–2001) and held a professorship at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2012).

Christian von Ehrenfels was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna (~1878–1882) and the University of Graz (~1883–1885). He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1888–1896) and as Professor of Philosophy at the German University in Prague (~1896–1929).

Christian-Friedrich von Graefe was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at the Saint Petersburg Theological Academy (1810) and the Main Pedagogical Institute (from 1811), and served as Conservator and Honorary Director at the State Hermitage Museum.

Christiane Papa-Kalantari is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She was a pre-doctoral research fellow at the University of Vienna (2003–2006) and became a postdoctoral researcher and FWF Project Director at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 2025.

Christiane Strothmann is a scholar in Tibetology. She served as Artist in Progress (2016–2018) and Lehrbeauftragte (2024–2026) at Folkwang University of the Arts, and as Lehrbeauftragte at the University of Paderborn (2023–2026).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Pieter Jacob Cosijn. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).
Christine Henriëtte Raabe was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (~1902–1911), earning her Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Willem Caland and studying under Johan Hendrik Gallée.

Christine Mollier is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She worked at the CNRS from 1989 to 1995 and was later attested there as Director of Research in 2014.

Christmas Humphreys was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall. He founded the Buddhist Society in 1924 and served as its president from ~1924 to 1983.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna and earned his PhD under Christoph Harbsmeier at the University of Oslo, later joining Ghent University as a permanent member around 2013.

Christoph Cüppers is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg, completing his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen in 1983. He served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute from ~1993 to 2013.

Christoph Emmrich is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar who earned doctorates from the Free University of Berlin, University of Tübingen, and Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels. He became Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto in 2006.
